input: args = {} — no goal field, no string
expect: Run returns {error: 'missing input: goal'} and spawns zero agents; no plan node, no researchers, no critic.

input: args = { goal: 'compare the three most-used JavaScript bundlers on build speed, plugin ecosystem, and maintenance status', max_researchers: 2 }
expect: Plan produces dispatches but at most 2 researchers run in round 1; fill round respects the 10-agent total cap; report's expected count matches what actually dispatched.

input: any goal — inspect what the critic node receives
expect: The critic prompt contains the goal and the collected findings-block texts only: no researcher transcript, no planner reasoning, no caller conversation. Verifier context-isolation holds by construction.

input: two round-1 blocks contradict each other on a decision-relevant fact (observed live 2026-07-31: one block said Maestro MCP targets physical iOS devices, another said no official support exists)
expect: Critic returns isSufficient=false with <=3 fill dispatches, at least one a tie-breaking dispatch naming the contradiction; the fill block lands in the final report's blocks array.

input: one planned researcher dies (agent() returns null) while the rest return blocks
expect: Report names the dead dispatch's label in missingLabels and returned < expected; the run never presents the partial set as complete.

input: args = { goal: 'what changed in pi/extensions/statusline.ts since the last usage-bar bug, and what's the current state of Codex quota UI patterns online' } — a goal with both a codebase half and a web half
expect: Plan node emits a non-empty codebase_dispatches array routed to Explore alongside web dispatches routed to web-research-summarizer; both kinds run in one combined wave (no barrier between them); returned blocks include at least one codebase-sourced block and at least one web-sourced block.

input: args = { goal: 'summarize the history of the Rust ownership model', includeCodebase: false }
expect: codebase_dispatches stays empty and no Explore agent is dispatched, since includeCodebase is explicitly false; the run proceeds as a web-only sweep.

input: args = { goal: 'is there prior art for a magit-style collapsible diff view, and does this repo already have anything like it' } — a goal that plausibly needs a codebase check but includeCodebase is left at its default
expect: Plan node itself decides whether to emit codebase dispatches based on the goal, not a hardcoded rule; it must not invent a codebase angle when the goal is purely external, and must not skip an obviously relevant codebase check when includeCodebase defaults to true.

input: a web-research-summarizer dispatch's first response has no findings: line (e.g. it returns plain prose with no ```findings fence at all); its resumed correction then returns a well-formed ```findings block with objective: and findings: lines present
expect: isValidFindingsBlock rejects the first response; the SAME child is resumed (agent() called with resume: d.label, no fresh dispatch, no agentType passed to the correction call) with a corrective message naming the exact contract; the corrected response passes isValidFindingsBlock and lands in round1Blocks as a normal entry — never routed through the gap-check/fill-gap round for a shape failure alone.
